corrected_value.authors: Webster, G. D., Urland, G. R., & Correll, J.
corrected_value.title: Can uniform color color aggression? Quasi-experimental evidence from professional ice hockey

decisions.location: Study III Introduction (lines 456-470); Study III Results (lines 595-647); Study III Discussion (lines 651-652); General Discussion (line 678); References (line 752).
decisions.quote:
There is only scant evidence to support the black-aggression hypothesis in the modern NHL ranks. Similar to our previous investigations, we failed to detect the effect when we conducted a nuanced analysis of the overall data (i.e., when accounting for the nested nature of the data) and also when we conducted a team-by-team analysis separately.
Also, we failed to find support for reduced aggression when wearing white uniforms (Webster et al., 2012) as we conducted comparisons within teams across eight seasons while ensuring the overall aggression in the league remained consistent (thus avoiding a history threat).
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. In Study III of 7bdaa130567dec72 (Goldschmied, Raphaeli, & Furley, 2026), 'Study III: Replication of National Hockey League Black Uniforms Effects in the Modern Era', the authors trace the NHL archival replication chain from Frank & Gilovich (1988) through Caldwell & Burger (2011) to Webster, Urland, & Correll (2012) (DOI 10.1177/1948550611418535). Study III directly retests Webster et al.'s (2012) NHL findings in an 8-season modern NHL dataset (2016/17-2023/24, 71,513 infringements), adopting Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) regression to account for nested team/season observations as emphasized by Webster et al., and explicitly testing both the black-uniform aggression hypothesis and Webster et al.'s (2012) specific finding of reduced aggression in white uniforms ('Also, we failed to find support for reduced aggression when wearing white uniforms (Webster et al., 2012) as we conducted comparisons within teams across eight seasons while ensuring the overall aggression in the league remained consistent'). Under the codebook rules (both as the closest study in the NHL replication chain and for its distinct white-uniform reverse effect), Webster et al. (2012) is a retested target distinct from shipped row 2625 (Frank & Gilovich, 1988). Luna's mechanical quote check failed only because of invisible zero-width spaces (U+200B) in the reference list DOI URL.
